title: Crowding and a storm
hook: Two model rules respond differently to crowding.

knows: Animals interact with other organisms and their surroundings.
doesNotKnow: In a toy model, food per animal falls when more animals share fixed food; a storm removes the same proportion at either density. Which rule is density-dependent?

misconception: One observation or model rule gives a complete answer about nature.
objective: In a toy model, food per animal falls when more animals share fixed food; a storm removes the same proportion at either density. Which rule is density-dependent?

claims.text: In a toy model, food per animal falls when more animals share fixed food; a storm removes the same proportion at either density. Which rule is density-dependent? Sharing fixed food changes the amount per animal as density changes. The stipulated storm fraction is fixed in both cases. Real weather and populations can behave differently.
claims.source: Unverified reference lead for independent check: OpenStax Biology 2e, ecology and populations, https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e . Exact claim-specific sources have not been verified.

claims.text: The panels depict a simplified illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
A toy model gives 12 food units to 3 or 6 animals equally. Which quantity changes with the number of animals? 12 divided among 3 gives 4 each; divided among 6 gives 2 each.

claims.text: In the toy display, 12 food units shared by 4 or 6 animals gives 3 or 2 units each; the storm fraction is stipulated as one half in both.

recall.question: A toy model gives 12 food units to 3 or 6 animals equally. Which quantity changes with the number of animals?
recall.why: 12 divided among 3 gives 4 each; divided among 6 gives 2 each.
